title: Worth it to Devlog?
author: JungleMobGames
selftext:
**You do not need to know how to build your entire idea before starting. You need to know what the next solvable problem is.** 

This is the message I want to send people watching my devlog on YouTube and TikTok. I want to inspire those who dream of building apps but have no prior coding experience and feel afraid to start. I believe the absence of a formal computer-science education shouldn’t be a barrier to building complex software. 

I’m building my first iOS game as a self-taught programmer going on 4 years now. The project developed into a vehicle for learning the complete architecture of a real multiplayer application, and it is intended to prove, through implementation rather than theory, that the skills required to design, develop, deploy, scale, and maintain a multiplayer game can be learned independently. 

**With the help of AI, of course.** 

A multiplayer game needs real players to match against, so I need to market the game and start a devlog.

But there’s a lot of hate out there about using AI tools to speedrun the programming of an app, so I’m worried about backlash, regardless if I am proficient at debugging and can explain what the code does in essence, and how all the parts of the system work in harmony. 

**To devlog or not to devlog, that is the question.**

comments.body: Dev log is inportant for indydev for wishlist

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: Build in public. It will snowball people into wanting to buy game and watch what your doing.

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: The hate comes from AI art not from AI dev tbh.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
That depends - is your goal to make a game, or is your goal to be a social media personality?

99% of potential purchasers do not give a shit how the sausage gets made, even moreso if you're Joe Rando and not some successful studio.

comments.author: BrownaroStudios
comments.body:
We have also contemplated this very question.  The problem for us is that if we were to document the development lifecycle, we would be documenting hours in the day.  Literally, an idea becomes reality too fast for us to document the progress we've made.   There is a point where we take the initial output and refine it but at that point it's a real game.  A real game that no one has seen or played before so there isn't a "woah, look at that improvement from the last video". 

I think the idea is sound but execution of it needs to be thought out and planned out in order to succeed.  Good luck!

comments.author: waypostmaster
comments.body: My dev blog is the primary product. The game just gives it content.

comments.author: GreenBlueStar
comments.body: How many successful indies have devlogs? That should answer your question. Or better yet how many devloggers successfully completed and published their games?
